assign.request: Adversarial critique of today's two headline deliverables: the homepage (/) and the blog (/blog/ + all six posts + section pages). Browse cold at 400/1920/3440, light and dark; read every post top to bottom; check the og: cards; judge sameness, dead air at 3440, images that don't earn their bytes, claims a hiring engineer would test. Rank 10-20 improvements, name 3 keepers.
assign.now: landed - 20 ranked items, 6 keeper shots, 3 keepers named
steps: read the source: homepage, blog shell, Post/Section, posts.js
read all six posts as prose

log.msg: method - private server on 8095 (:80 stays down), headless playwright: 30 shots at 400/1920/3440 light+dark, a geometry probe over all six posts, and a crawl of all 66 internal links reachable from / and /blog/. Read all 9 markdown files (~7,000 words) and all 7 stamped index.html shells as text.

#1 / (root index.html) - ships ZERO social/SEO meta: no description, no canonical, no og:*, no twitter:*, just charset + title 'lew42'. Every post has a perfect card; the one url a recruiter actually pastes unfurls as a bare link. Fix: extend meta.mjs to stamp / and /blog/ too, and give the front an og:image - S

#2 / (whole page) - nothing says WHO. h1 is about the framework, sidebar says LEW42, Resume is the 4th nav item, the blog's About says 'one person'. A recruiter landing cold cannot name the person, the role, or how to reach them without a click. Fix: one line under the hero - name, what you do, resume/contact link - S

#3 /blog/ai/claude-tooling/ opening sentence - 'Every page on this site was built by Claude'. On a job-prospecting site that hands the reader the conclusion 'he didn't build it', and 'every' is a claim the resume/fly/sandbox pages won't support. Fix: lead with what the HUMAN built - the brief, the file fence, the acceptance gate, the log - and make the agents the subject of the engineering, not the author of the portfolio - S

#4 / home-stage demo - emits 10 anchors, 4 of which 404: /web/html/ /web/css/ /web/js/ /web/svg/ (verified: left-click is intercepted and works, but direct load = 'Page Load Error 404 - nothing matches'). So middle-click, open-in-new-tab, copy-link and Googlebot all break on the site's flagship demo, from its highest-authority page. And the 404 they land on shows a DIFFERENT nav - Home Framework Web Alex Arya Castin Edric Michael, no Blog, no Resume. Fix: the demo already intercepts the click, so drop the real href (or point them at real /web/ pages) - S

#5 every post at 3440 - the fold is ~2,000px of empty grey. Prose measure ~700px hard left, rail 243px at x=3107, nothing between. First exhibit top at 3440: dashboard 1138, layout-generators 1284, how-this-blog-works 1061 - all BELOW the 1000px fold, so 3 of 6 posts open as one text column with 2,000px of nothing beside it. reading-page.md claims 'the ink now reaches within about 80px of the right edge instead of stopping 1400px short'; on those three folds it stops ~2,100px short. Fix: put something in the exhibit track above the first figure - standfirst as display type, a pull-quote, a key-facts block, or promote image: to a lead - M

#6 every post, dark mode - all 17 PNGs are light-UI captures, so on the dark theme each figure is a white slab against near-black: the harshest contrast on the page, on every post, at every width. Fix cheap: give .blog-exhibit img a light padded frame + border so the white reads as a mounted print rather than a hole. Fix right: dark variants for the 5 lead images - S / M

#7 SAMENESS - every post's fold is the identical six-element stack: crumb, 48px title, date, 2-line standfirst, one paragraph, H2 - and the H2 lands within a pixel of the same y on /ai/dashboard/ and /systems/panel-playground/ (y=583 at 3440). Five of six have no picture above the fold. The BODIES are not same-y (2-4 exhibits, one 3-part, one 2-part, four single, four different argument shapes) - it is template output for the first screen and real writing after it. Fix the opener, not the posts: let the manifest carry a per-post opener and use a different one per post - M

#8 /blog/ at 3440 - the magazine is vertically centered: content occupies y=298-702 of a 1000px viewport, ~300px dead above and ~300px below, plus the hero column's right half empty. The site's own reading-page.md says centering 'reads as a page that failed to load'; the front does it on the other axis. Fix: top-align the front and let the archive grow down - S

#9 /blog/ .blog-hero-title - computes to 31.9px at 1920 and 70.4px at 3440, because it is sized in cqw off a column that is narrow at the commonest desktop width. So at 1920 the FEATURED post's title is smaller than an ordinary post's own h1 (48px) and level with a section h1 - the lead does not lead exactly where most visitors see it. Fix: raise the clamp floor, or give the hero the full row below ~2000px - S

#10 .demo-note tint band stops short - CAUSE FOUND: demo.css line 81, `.demo-note { max-width: var(--measure) }` caps the very element that `.demo > .demo-note` paints `background: var(--tint)` and `border-top` on. Measured band/box: 400 350/352 (99%), 1280 541/546 (99%), 1920 576/619 (93%), 3440 648/1443 (45%, stopping 795px short). Verdict: invisible below ~1300px, GLARING at 3440 on the homepage's centrepiece; no post is affected (no post embeds a demo). Fix: full-bleed the tinted strip, cap the text inside it - S

#11 og:image shapes are wrong for a card - cards render 1.91:1 and crop. space-ruler.png 1525x343 = 4.45:1 and lead.png 3440x820 = 4.20:1 both letterbox to an illegible strip; board.png 1440x1000 = 1.44:1 loses its top and bottom. No og:image:width/height, no og:image:alt, no article:published_time. Fix: one 1200x630 card per post (the post's picture on a branded ground) plus the three tags - M

#12 every card everywhere - one-sentence descriptions clip mid-WORD at a 2-line clamp: 'booting the app for yo...', 'a space of layouts against a...', 'panel trees you drag, an...' - with 600px of empty space under every card. The manifest descriptions were written to be read whole. Fix: raise the clamp to 3 lines, or drop it - S

#13 / .home-hero - stretched to the demo's height (650px at 1920, 718px at 3440) around ~330px of content, so ~320px at 1920 and ~390px at 3440 sit empty in the fold's most valuable column. Fix: put the who-you-are line there (see #2), or let the hero hug and pull the posts up - S

#14 /blog/<section>/ - the weakest surface on the site: a title, one line, two cards, ~85% of the screen empty at 1920 and worse at 3440. And the `icon:` declared for all three sections in posts.js (widgets/handyman/smart_toy) is read by NOTHING - dead data in the file documented as the single source of truth. Fix: give the section page a real shape (icon, blurb, its posts, what is coming) or delete the index and let the rail be the archive - S/M

#15 /blog/framework/how-this-blog-works/ lead image - lead.png is a 3440-wide screenshot of THIS POST'S OWN reading page. Rendered at 1897px the type in it is ~7px and illegible, it costs 153KB, and it puts a picture of a rail 30px to the left of the real rail, which reads as a duplicated element. Fix: drop it, or replace it with the one thing the post is about that cannot otherwise be seen - the unfurled social card - S

#16 code goes wide only when it is wrapped in a figure - in layout-generators the opening layout-spec fence sits in the 630px reading column while a 1900px exhibit track sits empty beside it; three fences later in the same post float right because they are inside <figure class=blog-exhibit>. Same content type, two widths, no rule the reader can see. Fix: default a fence over N lines to the exhibit track, or state the rule in the readme and apply it - S

#17 .blog-rail is a stub - measured 228-384px tall against a 1000-1100px fold; layout-generators has 5 lines in a 243px column. It carries a ToC plus 'All X posts' and 'The blog' - never the next post, never the archive, never a word about the author. On a job-prospecting site the sticky right edge of every post is the one guaranteed-visible surface. Fix: next/previous pair + a two-line who-block with a resume link - S

#18 /blog/doc/ has three names and a title collision - the page's own title is 'Notes', the front rail links it as 'How this blog is built', and the site already has a top-level /notes/. Two of its four notes carry the SAME titles as the two published parts of how-this-blog-works ('Meta tags that actually work', 'The un-centered reading page') at different urls with no cross-link. Content differs (decision notes vs public prose) so it is not duplicate content, but a reader who finds one cannot know the other exists. Fix: one name, and cross-link each note to its published counterpart - S

#19 / at 400 - the first code a phone visitor sees is cut mid-string. The demo's code pane is a 350px scroll container holding 491px of content, ending on `p("Every element is a wor`, with no scrollbar, gradient or affordance. Fix: soft-wrap the demo code pane below 40em, or add a fade + hint - S

#20 '714 executable lines / 21 KB / 0 build steps / 0 runtime deps / 0 config files' - hardcoded string literals in framework/stats.js, quoted as measured fact in hello-lew42. wc -l on the four core files gives 1253, and the repo root holds package.json and wrangler.jsonc: the words 'executable', 'runtime' and 'config' are doing real work and the prose DOES link the method on /framework/versus/, which is honest. The weakness is that nothing recounts, so the number goes stale the moment core changes and the site's most testable claim rots silently. Fix: make check.mjs recount and fail on drift - S

KEEPER 1 - the reading layout at 1920. Prose hard left at a 40em measure, exhibits floating into the track beside them, rail pinned right. Best-composed screen on the site, and the float-not-grid decision is measurably right: no holes in the reading column at any exhibit, on any post. Do not turn it back into a grid.

KEEPER 2 - posts.js + meta.mjs. One copy of every title, date and description; the static shells stamped from it; --check fails on drift; a missing shell degrades to a missing card, never a broken page. Verified: all six posts' cards, rail entries and og tags agree exactly, escaped and charset-first. This is the thing to point at in an interview. Do not scatter it.

KEEPER 3 - the prose. ~7,000 words across 9 files with zero AI-generic filler. 'What it costs' names the losses out loud; 'What they actually share' opens with an audit that contradicts the intuitive answer; reading-page.md explains float-vs-grid with the measurement that decided it. Specific, mechanism-first, honest. Nothing in the next wave should punch this copy up. (Runner-up keeper: the 400px reading view - one honest column, generous type, clean.)

SAMENESS VERDICT: yes at the fold, no in the body. Five posts open with the identical six-element stack and two of them put their first H2 at the same y to the pixel; five of six show no picture above the fold. Below the fold they diverge properly - 2 to 4 exhibits, one 3-part, one 2-part, four single, and four genuinely different argument shapes. Fix the opener, not the posts.

OG-CARD VERDICT: mechanically correct and better than most hand-rolled blogs - all six posts stamp title/description/canonical/og/twitter from one manifest, escaped, charset first, with a fallback that degrades safely. Three real gaps: (a) the site ROOT has none at all, (b) /blog/ and the three sections are twitter:summary with no image, (c) two of six images are 4.20:1 and 4.45:1 and will render as illegible letterboxed strips, and none carries width/height/alt.

shot.caption: The AI dashboard at 3440: a 700px column of prose, a 243px rail, and ~2,000px of empty grey between them for the whole first screen.

assign.outcome:
**20 ranked improvements to the homepage and the blog, none applied — this task edited nothing outside its own directory.**

Browsed cold at 400 / 1920 / 3440 in light and dark (30 headless shots), read all nine markdown files as prose, read all seven stamped `index.html` shells, measured the geometry of all six posts, and crawled the 66 internal links reachable from `/` and `/blog/`.

**The five worth doing first**

1. `/index.html` ships **zero** social meta — no description, no canonical, no `og:*`. Every post has a perfect card; the one url a recruiter pastes has none. **S**
2. Nothing on `/` says who you are — the h1 is about the framework, the name is a logo, the résumé is the fourth nav item. **S**
3. *"Every page on this site was built by Claude"* opens the tooling post. On a job-prospecting site that hands the reader the wrong conclusion. **S**
4. The homepage demo emits four hrefs that **404** (`/web/html|css|js|svg/`). Left-click is intercepted so it feels fine; middle-click, open-in-new-tab and Googlebot are not. **S**
5. At 3440 three of six posts open with ~2,000px of empty grey between a 700px text column and a 243px rail — the exhibit track is empty above the first figure. **M**

**Three keepers the next wave must not break:** the reading layout at 1920 (prose hard left, exhibits floating beside it — float, not grid); `posts.js` + `meta.mjs` (one copy of every string, shells stamped from it, `--check` fails on drift); and the prose itself (~7,000 words, zero AI-generic filler).

**Sameness:** yes at the fold, no in the body — five posts open with the identical six-element stack and two put their first H2 at the same y to the pixel. Fix the opener, not the posts.

**og cards:** mechanically correct and better than most hand-rolled blogs. Three gaps — the site root has none, `/blog/` and the sections are `summary` with no image, and two of six images are 4.2:1 and 4.45:1 (illegible letterboxed strips).

All 20 items, with measurements and effort sizes, are the `#1`-`#20` log lines below. Six keeper screenshots are linked above.
